subject: Apex Health: clarification on private-deploy addendum (license / evidence)
messages:
From: Tom Riley <procurement@apexhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@apexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment addendum — license boundary and evidence ask

David — thanks for the demo last week. We are finalizing the Order Form and the Private Deployment Addendum but our legal and security teams have a couple of asks that we want to confirm before we redline:

1) License scope: Apex needs explicit language that runtime usage is limited to our single production VPC/cluster and any replication for DR must be in the same legal jurisdiction (US). Can Redwood confirm the proposed clause in Section 2.1 will satisfy that?

2) Evidence / escrow-like request: our security team would like an option to receive a sealed snapshot and an operator-access attestation in the event of termination. They do not require on-site witnessing but want to know the acceptable formats (forensic snapshot, VM image, or export package) and who signs the attestation.

3) Operator key custody: we want clarity on whether HSM-backed key escrow is supported, or if Redwood expects operator credentials to be rotated into customer custody.

Attached is our draft Order Form with the volume and SLOs. Can you route to legal for proposed language and let us know a timeline for a redline?

Thanks — Tom
Tom Riley
Senior Procurement Manager, Apex Health
procurement@apexhealth.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: Apex_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Riley <procurement@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 10:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — license boundary and evidence ask

Tom — appreciate the clear list. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

1) License scope: we can accept a jurisdiction-bound DR carve (same country) but we typically avoid hard restrictions on ephemeral test/engineering replicas used only for troubleshooting. Proposed path: include explicit production VPC restriction in the Order Form while allowing short-lived support replicas under documented change control. See proposed text attached (OrderForm_redline).

2) Evidence / snapshot: we support delivering a sealed forensic snapshot (S3-compatible archive + checksum) and a signed operator attestation. We do not typically deposit binaries into a third-party escrow, but we can provide a hashed snapshot plus a signed manifest and an operator proofing statement. We will need to confirm the exact deliverable format with Legal.

3) Operator keys: our recommended model is HSM-backed keys under Redwood custody with a notarized attestation at handback; alternatively customers can request key export and assume custody (extra fees and compliance steps).

Asking Marissa (legal) and Lauren (contracts) to propose redline language and confirm if this approach is acceptable. Tom — can you confirm whether Apex requires a standing deposit to an escrow agent or a running attestation only at termination? That will determine our exhibit.

Planned timeline: we'll get a legal redline back by EOD Thu (1/18) if we have clarity on escrow vs. attestation.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com
(650) 555-0119

Attachments: OrderForm_redline_notes.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Tom Riley <procurement@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — license boundary and evidence ask

Tom / David — looping in Lauren for procurement redline coordination. I reviewed Apex's draft and David's proposed approach. High-level legal position and suggested language:

- License scope: we can commit to production-only deployment in the Order Form (Section A) and add an exception for transient troubleshooting replicas limited to 72 hours and logged via a change-control ticket. Suggested language attached in redline PDF.

- Evidence / snapshot: Redwood can provide a sealed forensic export (sha256 checksummed archive) plus a signed operator attestation describing the operational procedures exercised. We object to placing executables with an escrow agent due to IP and security concerns. Suggested exhibit: "Sealed Snapshot & Attestation" (we propose an attestation template).

- Operator key custody: offer two options in Exhibit B — (1) Redwood HSM custody with notarized operator-attestation on handback, or (2) customer-managed key import with an additional security review and fees. Include an IP & access carveout so operator logs are retained for 90 days.

Please confirm: 1) whether Apex will accept the attestation + sealed snapshot exhibit (preferred), or 2) insist on deposit to an escrow agent (we will escalate pricing/tech viability). If escrow agent is insisted upon, we will need a 6-8 week engineering window to prepare a sanitized image and legal signoff.

I attach a draft attestation template and our redline for the addendum.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_Addendum_legal_redline.pdf, Sealed_Snapshot_Attestation_template.docx

From: Tom Riley <procurement@apexhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@apexhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 11:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — license boundary and evidence ask

Marissa — thanks for the detailed options. Apex legal prefers an "attestation + sealed snapshot" approach rather than depositing executables with an escrow agent. A few clarifications from our side:

- Snapshot format: an encrypted tarball with metadata (manifest.json) and sha256 checksums is acceptable.
- Attestation signer: we expect a named Redwood operations lead to sign the attestation (name + title + email). That person must be reachable during the evidence handback window.

We do not expect standing escrow; we only require the snapshot + attestation be producible within 30 days of termination notice.

If Redwood confirms the turnaround and that the attestation will be signed by a named operations contact, we can proceed to redline the Order Form and sign.

Tom
Tom Riley
Senior Procurement Manager, Apex Health
procurement@apexhealth.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Riley <procurement@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2028 16:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — license boundary and evidence ask

Tom — confirmed. Redwood accepts the sealed snapshot + signed attestation path with the following guardrails:

- Deliverable: encrypted tarball (s3 URL) + manifest.json + sha256 checksums; signed attestation from Redwood Operations Lead (name and contact below).
- SLA: Redwood will produce the deliverable within 30 calendar days of termination notice; if accelerated production is required we will quote engineering effort and potential fees.

Named signatory (Operations Lead):
Jordan Blake — Director, Operations (ops_lead@redwood.com)

Next steps: 1) Marissa, please incorporate the proposed Exhibit "Sealed Snapshot & Attestation" text into the addendum redline; 2) Lauren, please incorporate the 30-day production SLA into the Order Form; 3) Tom, if that meets Apex's needs please circulate the updated Order Form and we'll aim to finalize the signature package this week.

Thanks everyone — will follow up with the redline and a short executive summary for sign-off.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: Operator_Matrix_v1.xlsx (internal mapping of roles to signatories)
